subject.title: fix(exec-approvals): handle same-process sync/async lock contention

question: Should synchronous exec-approval reads remain fully ordered behind concurrent policy writes, or may they intentionally use the prior committed policy during an in-process update?
rationale: Process identity cannot distinguish genuine lock reentrancy from an unrelated async task, and choosing whether prior policy may authorize execution during revocation is an authorization-boundary contract.

options.title: Preserve write ordering
options.body: Restructure the contending call path or use owner-aware committed snapshots so independent readers wait for the policy update while true internal reentrancy remains possible.

options.title: Allow prior committed policy
options.body: Document and test that exec decisions may use the previous policy during concurrent updates, explicitly accepting delayed revocation semantics.

options.title: Pause this approach
options.body: Close or replace the PR if a bounded owner-aware solution cannot avoid both event-loop deadlock and authorization-order weakening.

recommendation.title: Preserve write ordering
recommendation.body: Restructure the contending call path or use owner-aware committed snapshots so independent readers wait for the policy update while true internal reentrancy remains possible.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision concerns the exec-approval security invariant most closely associated with their recent hardening work.
